though I have heard hundreds of thousands of sūtras from the Buddha and Mañjuśrī,
never have I heard such an inconceivable, freely supernormal, definitive reality sūtra.
As I understand the Buddha's meaning,
beings who hear this Dharma,
believe, understand, uphold, and recite it,
will undoubtedly attain this Dharma,
let alone practice as taught.
Such persons close all evil paths and open all good gates,
always protected and mindful by Buddhas,
subduing external teachings, destroying Māra's enmity,
cultivating bodhi, abiding securely in the seat of enlightenment,
treading the path walked by Tathāgatas.
World-Honored One,
for those who uphold, recite, and practice as taught,
I and my retinue will serve and make offerings.
Wherever this sūtra exists—in villages, cities, forests, or wilderness—
I and my retinue
will go to hear the Dharma.
We will make unbelievers believe,
and protect those who already believe."
The Buddha said,
"Excellent, excellent,
Lord of Gods!
As you have said,
I rejoice with you.
This sūtra extensively explains the inconceivable Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi of past, future, and present Buddhas.
Therefore, Lord of Gods,
any good man or woman
who upholds, recites, and makes offerings to this sūtra thereby makes offerings to past, future, and present Buddhas.
Lord of Gods,
suppose the three-thousand great thousand worlds were filled with Tathāgatas
like stands of sugarcane, bamboo, rice, hemp, or trees,
and a good man or woman
for an eon or less
respectfully honored, praised, and made offerings to them,
and after their parinirvāṇa,
erected seven-jeweled stūpas for each whole-body relic,
each as vast as a universe, high as Brahmā heavens, with ornate banners,
offering all finest flowers, incense, garlands, banners, music, and supreme subtleties."
Whether for one kalpa or less than one kalpa, if one makes offerings during that time,
what do you think, O Celestial Emperor?
Would the merit planted by that person be considerable?
Śakro Devānām Indra replied,
Very much so, World-Honored One.
Their merit and virtue, if spoken of for hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, could not be exhausted.
The Buddha told the Celestial Emperor,
You should know that if a good man or good woman
hears this inconceivable liberation sutra, believes, understands, accepts, upholds, reads, recites, and practices it, their merit surpasses that.
Why is this?
Because the enlightenment of all buddhas arises from this.
The characteristic of enlightenment is immeasurable.
For this reason, the merit is immeasurable.
The Buddha told the Celestial Emperor,
In the past, during immeasurable, countless kalpas,

there was a buddha in the world named King of Medicine Thus Come One, Worthy of Offerings, Rightly and Universally Awakened, Perfect in Clarity and Conduct, Well-Gone, Understander of the World, Unsurpassed One, Tamer of Humans, Teacher of Gods and Humans, Buddha, World-Honored One.
His world was called Great Adornment,
and the kalpa was named Adornment.
The buddha's lifespan was twenty small kalpas.
His voice-hearer disciples numbered thirty-six billion nayutas,
and his bodhisattva disciples numbered twelve billion.
Celestial Emperor,
at that time, there was a wheel-turning sage king named Precious Canopy,
fully endowed with the seven treasures, ruling over the four continents.
The king had a thousand sons,
upright, brave, and strong, capable of subduing enemies.
At that time, Precious Canopy and his retinue made offerings to King of Medicine Thus Come One,
providing all comforts for a full five kalpas.
After five kalpas had passed, he told his thousand sons,
You too should, like me, wholeheartedly make offerings to the buddha.
Thereupon, the thousand sons accepted their father's command,
and made offerings to King of Medicine Thus Come One,
again providing all comforts for a full five kalpas.
One of the king's sons, named Moon Canopy,
sat alone in contemplation,
wondering, "Is there any offering superior to this?"
Through the buddha's spiritual power, a celestial voice in the sky said,
Good man,
the offering of the Dharma surpasses all offerings.
He then asked,
What is meant by the offering of the Dharma?
The celestial voice said,
You may go and ask King of Medicine Thus Come One,
who will extensively explain to you the offering of the Dharma.
Immediately, Prince Moon Canopy went to King of Medicine Thus Come One, bowed at the buddha's feet,
stepped back, stood to one side, and addressed the buddha, saying,
World-Honored One,
among all offerings, the offering of the Dharma is supreme.
What constitutes the offering of the Dharma?
The Buddha said,
Good man,
the offering of the Dharma means
the profound sutras spoken by all buddhas,
which are difficult for all the world to believe and accept,
subtle, hard to perceive, pure, and undefiled,
not attainable merely through discrimination and thought,
encompassed within the bodhisattva's treasury of Dharma,
sealed by the dhāraṇī seal,
leading to non-retrogression, accomplishing the six pāramitās,
skillfully discerning meanings, conforming to the Dharma of enlightenment,
supreme among all sutras, entering great compassion,
free from all demonic affairs and erroneous views,
conforming to the Dharma of dependent origination,
without self, without person, without being, without life,
empty, signless, wishless, unproduced,
enabling beings to sit at the site of enlightenment and turn the Dharma wheel,
praised by all gods, dragons, spirits, gandharvas, and others,
enabling beings to enter the treasury of the Buddha's Dharma,
encompassing all wisdom of the sages,
expounding the path practiced by all bodhisattvas,
based on the meaning of the true reality of all dharmas,
clearly proclaiming the Dharma of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, selflessness, and nirvana,
capable of saving all beings who have broken precepts,
causing fear in all demons, non-Buddhists, and those attached to greed,
praised by all buddhas and sages,
turning away from the suffering of birth and death, showing the joy of nirvana,
spoken by all buddhas of the ten directions and three times.
If one hears such sutras,
believes, understands, accepts, upholds, reads, and recites them,
and with skillful means, for the sake of all beings, explains them distinctly, revealing them clearly,
for the sake of protecting the Dharma,
this is called the offering of the Dharma.
Furthermore, practicing in accordance with the Dharma as taught,
following the twelve links of dependent origination,
free from all erroneous views, attaining the patience of non-arising,
determined that there is no self and no beings,
yet regarding causes, conditions, and effects,
without opposition, without contention, free from all possessiveness,
relying on the meaning, not the words,
relying on wisdom, not consciousness,
relying on the definitive sutras, not the non-definitive,
relying on the Dharma, not the person,
following the characteristics of the Dharma, without entering, without returning,
because ignorance is ultimately extinguished,
formations are also ultimately extinguished,
up to because birth is ultimately extinguished,
old age and death are also ultimately extinguished.
Contemplating in this way,
the twelve links of dependent origination have no exhausting characteristic,
and views no longer arise.
This is called the supreme offering of the Dharma.
The Buddha told the Celestial Emperor,
Prince Moon Canopy, from King of Medicine Buddha,
hearing such Dharma, attained the patience of compliance.
He then removed his precious robes and adornments,
offered them to the buddha, and said,
World-Honored One,
after the Thus Come One's nirvana, I will practice the offering of the Dharma and protect the true Dharma.
I pray that with your majestic power, you will compassionately establish me,
enabling me to subdue demonic adversaries and cultivate the bodhisattva path.
The Buddha, knowing his profound intention,
predicted to him,
You, in the final age, will protect the citadel of the Dharma.
Celestial Emperor,
At that time, Prince Moon Canopy, seeing the purity of the Dharma,
and hearing the buddha's prediction, left home with faith,
cultivated and accumulated wholesome dharmas, and with diligence, before long,
attained the five spiritual powers and realized the bodhisattva path,
gained dhāraṇīs and unceasing eloquence.
After the buddha's nirvana, using the power of his spiritual powers, retention, and eloquence,
for ten small kalpas, he propagated the Dharma wheel turned by King of Medicine Thus Come One.
The bhikṣu Moon Canopy, protecting the Dharma, diligently practiced with vigor,
and in that very life, transformed hundreds of trillions of people,
establishing them in non-retrogression on anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Fourteen nayutas of people deeply aroused the mind of śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas,
and immeasurable beings were born in the heavens.
Celestial Emperor,
Was King Precious Canopy of that time someone else?
He is now the buddha named Precious Flame Thus Come One.
His thousand sons are the thousand buddhas of the present Fortunate Kalpa,
starting with Krakucchanda Buddha,
and the last Thus Come One is named Rucika.
The bhikṣu Moon Canopy is myself.
Thus, O Celestial Emperor,
you should know this essential point:
the offering of the Dharma is superior to all offerings,
the foremost, the highest, the unequaled.
Therefore, O Celestial Emperor,
you should make the offering of the Dharma to make offerings to the buddha.
Thereupon, the Buddha addressed Bodhisattva Maitreya, saying,
Maitreya,
I now entrust to you
the anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi Dharma collected over immeasurable billions of countless kalpas.
Such sutras, after the buddha's nirvana, in the latter age,
you should widely propagate and spread throughout Jambudvīpa with your spiritual power, without allowing them to be cut off.
Why is this?
Because in the future world, there will be good men and good women,
as well as gods, dragons, spirits, gandharvas, rākṣasas, and others,
who arouse the mind of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi and delight in the great Dharma.
If they do not hear such sutras, they will lose the benefit of goodness.
When such people hear these sutras,
they will surely believe and delight greatly, arouse rare minds, receive them with utmost respect, and extensively explain them according to what benefits beings.
Maitreya, you should know
that bodhisattvas have two characteristics.
What are the two?
First, those who prefer elaborate phrases and ornate expressions.
Second, those who do not fear profound meanings and can truly enter them.
Those who prefer elaborate phrases and ornate expressions—know that they are newly initiated bodhisattvas.
Those who, regarding such undefiled, unattached, profoundly deep sutras, have no fear and can enter them,
hearing them, purify their minds, accept, uphold, read, recite, and practice as taught,
know that they are long-cultivated in the path.
Maitreya,
there are also two dharmas
that characterize new learners
who cannot be steadfast in the profound Dharma.
What are the two?
First, when they hear profound sutras they have not heard before,
they become frightened, doubtful, and cannot accept them,
slandering and disbelieving, saying such things as,
"I have never heard this before; where did it come from?"
Second, if there are those who protect and explain such profound sutras,
they refuse to draw near, make offerings, or show respect,
or sometimes speak of their faults.
Having these two dharmas,
know that they are newly initiated bodhisattvas,
who harm themselves,
and cannot tame their minds in the profound Dharma.
Maitreya,
there are also two dharmas
whereby bodhisattvas, though they believe and understand the profound Dharma,
still harm themselves and cannot attain the patience of non-arising.
What are the two?
First, looking down upon newly initiated bodhisattvas and not instructing them.
Second, though understanding the profound Dharma, still grasping at characteristics and discriminating.
These are the two dharmas.
Bodhisattva Maitreya, hearing this, addressed the Buddha, saying,
World-Honored One,
How unprecedented!
As the Buddha has said,
I will avoid such evils and uphold the anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi Dharma collected by the Thus Come One over countless, immeasurable kalpas.
In the future world, for good men and good women seeking the Great Vehicle, I will ensure they obtain such sutras,
grant them the power of mindfulness,
so they may accept, uphold, read, recite, and extensively explain them to others.
World-Honored One,
If in the latter age there are those who can accept, uphold, read, recite, and explain to others,
know that they are all established through Maitreya's spiritual power.
The Buddha said,
Excellent, excellent, Maitreya,
as you have said.
The Buddha rejoices in your words.
Thereupon all the bodhisattvas joined their palms and addressed the Buddha:
"We too, after the Tathāgata's parinirvāṇa,
will widely proclaim and disseminate the Dharma of Anuttarā Samyaksaṃbodhi throughout the lands of the ten directions.
Furthermore, we shall guide all who expound the Dharma to enable them to obtain this sūtra."
Then the Four Heavenly Kings addressed the Buddha:
"World-Honored One,
wherever this sūtra is present—in cities, towns, villages, forests, or wilderness—
where there are those who read, recite, and expound this sūtra,
we shall lead our retinues to their location to listen to the Dharma and protect such persons.
Within a hundred yojanas radius, we will prevent any opportunistic seekers from finding advantage."
At that time, the Buddha told Ānanda:
"Uphold this sūtra and widely proclaim and disseminate it."
Ānanda replied, "So be it.
I have already received and upheld its essentials.
World-Honored One,
by what name should this sūtra be called?"
The Buddha said:
"Ānanda,
this sūtra is called 'The Vimalakīrti Nirdeśa'
and also 'The Gateway to the Inconceivable Liberation.'
Thus should you uphold it."
When the Buddha had finished speaking this sūtra,
the elder Vimalakīrti,
Mañjuśrī,
Śāriputra,
Ānanda, and others,
along with all the heavenly beings, asuras, and the entire great assembly,
hearing what the Buddha had proclaimed, all rejoiced greatly.
